age.evidence: A total of 48 male DCXCreERT2::TdTOM lox/lox mice with a C57BL/6 genetic background, aged postnatal day 45-70, were used in this study.

sex.evidence: A total of 48 male DCXCreERT2::TdTOM lox/lox mice ... The decision to use only male animals was based on prior evidence...

dosing.evidence: Mice in all DMT-treated groups received a single intraperitoneal injection of 30 mg/kg DMT ... diluted fresh in saline (1:9, DMSO:saline) on the day of treatment to reach 30 mg/kg dose.

handling.evidence: Non-UCMS mice underwent gentle handling during the same period as the stressors.

group_housing.evidence: All mice were housed under standard conditions, including a 12 h light/dark cycle, with food and water available ad libitum.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All mice were housed under standard conditions, including a 12 h light/dark cycle

assays.assay_description: 10 min session in a 40 × 32 × 15 cm open arena; measured distance travelled and time in center zone using AnimalTA tracking + MATLAB analysis.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of 30 mg/kg DMT

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus habituation described for OFT

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were always placed at the center of the arena

food_restriction.evidence: Standard OFT apparatus; no food in the arena during testing

water_restriction.evidence: Standard OFT apparatus; no water in the arena during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: The OFT was performed on day 4 [of behavioral testing]; DMT was given on day 58 and behavioral testing began on day 73, so OFT occurred ~15 days post-dose.

sample_size.evidence: n's for OFT not explicitly stated separately

outcomes.summary: No significant differences between UCMS saline, Non-UCMS controls, or any treatment group in distance travelled or time spent in the center.
outcomes.statistics: one-way ANOVA, no significant differences reported
outcomes.evidence: In the OFT (Supplementary Fig. 3A-C), we did not observe any statistically significant differences between UCMS saline-treated mice, Non-UCMS controls, or any of the treatment groups

B1_num_measures.evidence: distance travelled and time spent in the center

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total summed measures, no within-session time-course

E1_environment_type.evidence: open arena with dimensions of 40 cm × 32 cm × 15 cm

E6_spatial.evidence: Open arena with virtual center zone

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the OFT arena

D1_continuity.evidence: OFT performed on day 4 of behavioral testing

D5_followup.evidence: OFT performed ~15 days after DMT injection

assays.assay_description: 10 min session in elevated cross-shaped maze (52 cm above ground; arms 62 × 6.5 cm; closed arms 20 cm walls); measured % time in open arms and manually-scored head dips.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of 30 mg/kg DMT

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus habituation described for EPM

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were placed in the center of the maze, facing an open arm

time_to_assay.evidence: EPM was conducted on day 15 of behavioral testing; DMT administered on day 58 and testing began day 73

sample_size.evidence: n's for EPM not explicitly reported

outcomes.summary: No significant differences among groups in percentage of time in open arms or number of head dips; UCMS and DMT treatments did not detectably alter anxiety-like behaviour in the EPM.
outcomes.evidence: in the EPM ... ANOVA analysis revealed no significant differences across treatment groups, UCMS saline, or Non-UCMS controls in terms of the percentage of time spent in the open arms. We also found no significant differences in the number of head dips

B1_num_measures.evidence: % time in open arms and number of head dips

B4_ethological.evidence: Head dips are apparatus-specific exploratory measure, not natural ethological behaviour per rubric

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are not classified as shelter per rubric

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are extensions of central platform; not separate compartments per rubric

D1_continuity.evidence: EPM conducted on day 15 of testing

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each animal was tested for 10 min

assays.assay_description: Home-cage two-bottle choice test (1% sucrose vs water) over 48 h, with bottle positions switched at 24 h. Performed at baseline, post-UCMS, and post-treatment. Anhedonia measured as % sucrose consumed.

application_type.evidence: DMT (30 mg/kg, i.p.) administered before post-treatment SPT

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were first habituated to drinking water from two bottles for 24 h

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice singly housed in home cage during testing

food_restriction.evidence: food and water available ad libitum during home-cage testing

water_restriction.evidence: Two bottles (water and sucrose) accessible throughout 48 h

time_to_assay.evidence: SPT performed at baseline (pre-UCMS), post-UCMS (pre-treatment), and post-treatment (days 10-13 of behavioral testing)

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes (after exclusions) given in Fig. 2: Non-UCMS (n = 8), UCMS (n = 21), UCMS Fluoxetine (n = 8), UCMS DMT-d28 (n = 5); post-treatment SPT all groups n = 8

outcomes.summary: All DMT-treated groups (DMT, DMT+Iso, DMT-d28) significantly increased sucrose preference vs UCMS saline (all p < 0.0001), reversing anhedonia. Fluoxetine produced a modest but significant increase (p = 0.0179). DMT-d28 had already reversed anhedonia by the post-UCMS assessment.
outcomes.statistics: DMT, DMT+Iso, DMT-d28 vs UCMS-saline all p < 0.0001; Fluoxetine p = 0.0179; DMT vs Fluoxetine p = 0.0029
outcomes.evidence: All DMT-treated groups, including DMT alone, DMT under isoflurane, and DMT-d28, exhibited significantly higher sucrose preference compared to UCMS saline controls (all p < 0.0001)

B5_social.evidence: Individually housed during testing, no social construct

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were individually housed beginning on the habituation day and remained singly housed throughout the test period

E2_shelter.evidence: Standard home cage, no shelter described

E3_bedding.evidence: Home-cage testing implies standard bedding present

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material described in test

E6_spatial.evidence: Single home cage; two bottles do not constitute separate compartments

E8_food_water.evidence: Two bottles (water + 1% sucrose) available throughout test

D1_continuity.evidence: SPT performed at baseline, post-UCMS, and post-treatment

D2_session_duration.evidence: Total volume consumed over the 48 h testing period was recorded

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline SPT performed before UCMS and before treatment

D5_followup.evidence: Post-treatment SPT performed >24 h after DMT injection

assays.assay_description: Mice suspended by tail (with anti-climb cuff) 45 cm above ground in a 60 × 15 × 70 cm box; immobility scored by DeepLabCut pose estimation and custom Python analysis.

application_type.evidence: DMT (30 mg/kg, i.p.) administered before TST

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus habituation described for TST

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were suspended by their tails ... gently secured with adhesive tape to a wooden shaft

time_to_assay.evidence: TST conducted on day 7 of behavioral testing; DMT administered on day 58 and testing began day 73 (~20 days post-dose)

sample_size.evidence: Non-UCMS (n = 6), UCMS Saline (n = 5), UCMS Fluoxetine (n = 6), UCMS DMT (n = 7), UCMS DMT + Iso (n = 6), UCMS DMT-d28 (n = 7)

outcomes.summary: All DMT regimens (DMT, DMT+Iso, DMT-d28) and fluoxetine significantly reduced TST immobility compared with UCMS-saline, with no significant differences among treatments.
outcomes.statistics: DMT p < 0.0001; DMT+Iso p < 0.0001; Fluoxetine p = 0.0001; DMT-d28 p = 0.0002 (vs UCMS saline)
outcomes.evidence: all tested treatments, i.e., DMT (p < 0.0001), DMT+Iso (p < 0.0001), fluoxetine (p = 0.0001), and DMT-d28 (p = 0.0002), effectively reduced immobility compared to UCMS saline controls

B4_ethological.evidence: Immobility is not an ethological behaviour per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: DeepLabCut (DLC) was used for tracking, and the outputs were analyzed with a custom-made Python script

D1_continuity.evidence: TST performed on day 7 of behavioral testing only

D2_session_duration.evidence: TST duration not explicitly stated; standard TST is typically <15 min

D5_followup.evidence: TST performed >24 h after DMT injection

assays.assay_name: Radial Arm Maze - Delayed Non-Matching to Place
assays.assay_description: 8-arm radial maze (arms 30 × 8 × 30 cm, central 20 cm platform) with sample + test phases (~20 s delay, maze rotated). 4 trials/day × 15 days × 3 separation conditions (S2, S3, S4); reward = Fruit Loop. Correct first-choice and errors scored manually.

application_type.evidence: DMT (30 mg/kg, i.p.) administered before RAM testing

setup_habituation.evidence: animals had limited access to food during the 15 days of testing and were habituated to the reward five days prior to maze training

setup_restrain.evidence: Animal moved freely through the maze arms

food_restriction.evidence: To ensure task motivation, animals had limited access to food during the 15 days of testing

water_restriction.evidence: No water provided in maze during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: RAM testing spanned days 73-88 (post-treatment) — at least 15 days after DMT injection on day 58

outcomes.summary: UCMS-saline mice performed worse than Non-UCMS in the highest-difficulty condition (S2). DMT, DMT+Iso, and fluoxetine post-UCMS significantly improved S2 performance; DMT-d28 (administered during stress) did not rescue cognitive deficits. No group differences at lower difficulties (S3/S4).
outcomes.statistics: UCMS vs Non-UCMS p = 0.0165; DMT p < 0.0001; DMT+Iso p = 0.0108; Fluoxetine p = 0.0007 (vs UCMS-saline); two-way RM ANOVA treatment p < 0.0001, training p < 0.0001
outcomes.evidence: animals treated with fluoxetine (p = 0.0007), DMT (p < 0.0001), and DMT+Iso (p = 0.0108) displayed significantly enhanced performance compared to the UCMS-saline group ... the DMT-d28 group did not significantly differ from saline-treated animals (p = 0.7273)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Correct first attempts and errors scored across S2, S3, S4 conditions

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Learning analyzed across days, not within-session time-course

B6_cognitive.evidence: DNMP-RAM task assessed cognitive function, specifically reference and working memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: All data were recorded manually during the experiment by an experienced researcher

E5_enrichment.evidence: Reward wells are task stimuli, not enrichment

E6_spatial.evidence: 8 arms connected to central platform with removable doors

E8_food_water.evidence: Fruit Loop reward placed in arms during trials

D1_continuity.evidence: 4 trials/day over 15 days for each separation condition

D2_session_duration.evidence: Test trials up to 4 min + correction phase up to 10 min × 4 trials/day

D5_followup.evidence: RAM testing began ~15 days post-DMT and continued for 15 more days

judge_notes: Both candidates identified the same 5 behavioural assays (OFT, EPM, SPT, TST, DNMP-RAM); no merges or drops were needed.
For time_to_assay, behavioural testing began on day 73 (~15 days after the day-58 DMT injection), so all assays fall in long_term_over7d, overriding both candidates' early_2to24h.
B7 for TST scored 1 (DeepLabCut pose estimation), overriding qwen's earlier consistency — gptoss had this correct.
B5 for SPT scored 0 (anhedonia is a hedonic/reward construct, not a social construct as gptoss claimed).
SPT D6 scored 1 — the 48 h session clearly exceeds 6 h, even though measurements are taken at endpoints (the test session itself spans the full duration).
SPT E3 scored 1 (home-cage bedding present) and E6 scored 0 (a single home cage with two bottles is not multiple compartments per rubric).
DNMP-RAM E1 scored 0 (standard cognitive apparatus, not an enriched arena) and E5 scored 0 (reward wells are task stimuli per rubric).
DNMP-RAM D3 scored 3 (15+ days), overriding gptoss's misapplied category label.
Handling scored 'yes' at study level because Non-UCMS controls underwent gentle handling explicitly ("Non-UCMS mice underwent gentle handling during the same period as the stressors").
